polities.how: The ivory trade armed the chiefs.
polities.next: German conquest from 1890.

polities.t: Russian Turkestan and the protected khanates
polities.gov: Russian governorate-general of Turkestan from 1867; Bukhara and Khiva as protectorates
polities.head: Russian governors-general; the Emir of Bukhara; the Khan of Khiva
polities.rel: Sunni Islam
polities.econ: Cotton for Russian mills; railways from 1888
polities.now: Russia's colonial Central Asia, with the emirs kept as clients, cotton imposed, and the revolt of 1916 against conscription crushed.
polities.how: Conquest between 1865 and 1884.
polities.next: The Bolsheviks abolish the khanates in 1920 and draw the Soviet republics in 1924.

polities.gov: Russian viceroyalty of the Caucasus; three independent republics 1918 to 1920
polities.head: Russian viceroys; the Georgian Menshevik republic; the Armenian and Azerbaijani republics
polities.rel: Georgian and Armenian Orthodox; Shia Islam in Azerbaijan
polities.econ: Baku's oil, the world's largest field around 1900; Georgian manganese
polities.now: Russia annexed Georgia in 1801 and the Persian provinces by 1828; Baku's oil boom made the region the empire's industrial south; three republics declared independence in 1918.
polities.how: Russian conquest, the 1905 revolution's violence, the 1918 collapse.
polities.next: The Red Army takes all three by 1921; Soviet republics until 1991.

polities.t: Kingdom of Iraq under British mandate
polities.gov: British mandate 1920 to 1932; Hashemite monarchy under Faisal I; independent in 1932 with British bases
polities.head: Faisal I (1921 to 1933); Ghazi; the regent Abd al-Ilah; Nuri al-Said
polities.rel: Shia majority, Sunni ruling elite, Kurds, Jews, Christians
polities.econ: Oil at Kirkuk from 1927; the Iraq Petroleum Company
polities.now: Three Ottoman provinces made a kingdom for Britain's wartime ally Faisal after the 1920 revolt, with oil concessions and air bases as the price of independence.
polities.how: The Mosul question, the 1920 revolt, the Cairo conference of 1921.
polities.next: The 1941 pro-Axis coup is reversed by British troops; the monarchy falls in 1958.

polities.gov: French colony from Brazza's treaties of 1880; part of French Equatorial Africa from 1910
polities.head: Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza; French governors
polities.rel: Catholic missions; Kongo religion
polities.econ: Rubber and ivory concessions; the Congo-Océan railway
polities.now: The north bank of the Congo taken by Brazza for France in 1880, governed through concession companies, and the capital of Free French Africa in 1940.
polities.how: Brazza's treaty with the Teke king Makoko; the concession regime.
polities.next: Independence in August 1960.

polities.gov: Marxist one-party state 1969 to 1991; civil war 1997; Denis Sassou Nguesso president 1979 to 1992 and since 1997
polities.head: Fulbert Youlou; Marien Ngouabi; Denis Sassou Nguesso
polities.rel: Christian majority
polities.econ: Oil, timber; Chinese loans
polities.now: Congo-Brazzaville, across the river from Kinshasa, an oil state ruled for most of four decades by Sassou Nguesso, who regained power by civil war in 1997.
polities.how: Independence, the 1963 revolution, Marxism, the 1992 election, the 1997 war.
polities.next: Succession and oil debt.

polities.gov: No sovereignty: seven territorial claims frozen by the Antarctic Treaty of 1959; governed by consensus of the treaty parties
polities.head: The Antarctic Treaty Consultative Meeting
polities.rel: None
polities.econ: Science; fishing in the Southern Ocean regulated; mining banned by the 1991 protocol
polities.now: The only continent without a state, reserved for science and peace by treaty since 1959, with claims by Britain, Argentina, Chile, Norway, France, Australia and New Zealand set aside.
polities.how: Exploration from 1820; the race to the pole in 1911; the International Geophysical Year of 1957 to 1958.
polities.next: The mining ban comes up for review in 2048; China and Russia press for fishing rights.

polities.gov: Chinese control from 1950; the Tibet Autonomous Region from 1965; the Dalai Lama's government in exile at Dharamsala
polities.head: The Dalai Lama in exile since 1959; Communist Party secretaries of the region
polities.rel: Tibetan Buddhism under state control; monasteries destroyed in the Cultural Revolution, partly rebuilt
polities.pop: About 3.6 million in the region; 6 million Tibetans in China
polities.econ: Subsidised by Beijing; the railway from 2006; mining and tourism; Han migration
polities.now: Invaded in 1950, in revolt in 1959, Tibet lost its theocracy and most of its monasteries; the Dalai Lama's exile and the 2008 protests keep the question alive while Beijing settles Han migrants and prepares to name his successor.
polities.how: The 1951 agreement, the 1959 rising, the Cultural Revolution, the 2008 protests.
polities.next: The succession to the Dalai Lama, who is in his nineties.

polities.gov: Tribal confederations; the Sharifs of Mecca under Mamluk then Ottoman overlordship; Zaydi imams in Yemen; Ibadi Oman
polities.head: Sharifs of Mecca; tribal shaykhs
polities.cap: Mecca; Riyadh a small oasis town
polities.rel: Sunni Islam; the Wahhabi movement from 1744
polities.econ: Pilgrimage, pastoralism, pearling on the Gulf coast
polities.now: A peninsula of tribes and oases with the holy cities under distant Ottoman sovereignty, where Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab's reform movement and the Al Saud of Diriyah join forces in 1744.
polities.how: Ottoman suzerainty from 1517; the Wahhabi pact.
polities.next: The first Saudi state takes Mecca in 1803.

polities.gov: Constitutional monarchy; British protectorate 1900 to 1970; democratic reforms in 2010
polities.head: Kings of the Tupou dynasty; Tupou VI
polities.rel: Methodist and other Christian churches
polities.econ: Remittances, agriculture, aid
polities.now: The only Pacific kingdom never colonised, which kept its monarchy under British protection and widened its parliament in 2010.
polities.how: Tupou I's constitution of 1875; the 1900 treaty.
polities.next: Climate change and emigration.
